newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. envoy asks warring Afghans to spare civilians.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy asks warring Afghans to spare civilians.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl urged Afghan factions battling for control of Kabul on Wednesday to stop fighting and spare civilian lives.
"My message is: spare the lives of the innocent civilians who have already suffered enough from years of useless bloodshed," said Holl, who took up his post in July.

"I am once again urgently appealing to all the factions...to observe an immediate ceasefire, refrain from further use of military force to resolve their problems and to begin earnestly and seriously negotiations for a lasting political settlement and peace in their country," he said in a statement.
He also urged "those countries with influence in Afghanistan to persuade the warring parties to abandon the course of war and cooperate with the United Nations" in the search for peace.
The Taleban said they were fighting government forces on the eastern edge of Kabul on Wednesday after capturing the town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) east of the capital, overnight.
U.N. staff in Kabul said there were chaotic scenes in the city with tanks and military vehicles on the move as the Taleban forces advanced. They had no word on casualties.
The Taleban, who emerged from the obscurity of religious schools in Pakistan two years ago, have been fighting to oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.
